placements.title: Directing what is known shifts from recording to disowning
placements.frame: Does this expression claim authority to decide what counts as known, forgotten, or historically true about a specific record — asserting control over the record itself rather than arguing from evidence within it?
placements.why: The graph structure and strata are both empty (this is the first envelope), and the perspective's map/index confirm no existing coverage of the Kestrelwood spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, or Quill Ashgrove's calibration work at any grain (pass-2 resolved all three segments as 'new' for that reason). With nothing to reuse, the question is whether this content clears the narrative grain test rather than being a one-off fact. It does: src-1 and src-2 are imperatives commanding erasure of a specific technical/historical record, and src-3 rewrites that record by flat assertion ('never calibrated'). Held together (as the position pass already did, treating all three as one authority-ranking move), this is not itself a fact about calibration — it is a recurring thematic pattern (asserting authority over what a record contains by directing forgetting or by fiat-denial) that future envelopes making similar erasure/denial moves would keep feeding, regardless of which instrument or fact is at stake. That clears the 'true beyond the words it describes' bar, so it earns a leaf rather than being folded as evidence under some other theme that doesn't yet exist. Nothing in the empty structure or strata is even close enough to warrant an INSPIRED lineage edge, so this mints standalone with no forced parent — consistent with a first-envelope repo where no hub yet exists to hold it.
